reviewed_controller_contract.batch_identity: Distinct occasion/target SHA IDs become native row.id. Repeat bodies can be identical while ownership/request identities remain separate. No body hash or HTTP arrival ordinal alone identifies a sample.
reviewed_controller_contract.completion: Actual report and full artifact inventory are sealed and tied to original owner; deactivation reason anchors the seal SHA. A seal with active owner is an interrupted/unanchored refusal, not automatically adopted.
reviewed_controller_contract.locking: Existing exclusive PID-only running.lock pattern refuses concurrent or retained interrupted execution. It does not establish writer ownership, process health or permission to delete a stale lock.
reviewed_controller_contract.outputs: Complete NativeSession status is insufficient by itself: require exact once-only target population, literal task/answer preservation, matching per-target 2/4/10 partition cardinality, nonboolean nonnegative labels and matching distinct count.
reviewed_controller_contract.prepare: Four deterministic original owners under the supplied shared authority. All batch metadata, supplied native bytes, descriptors, actual source files and selected components are frozen before execution; prepare itself does not read keys or send requests.
reviewed_controller_contract.recovery: New attempt directories use original generations only and fresh native scratch/cache. Same owner replays exact retained raw receipts; a fresh occasion uses a separate owner. No owner replacement, unknown hold release or dynamic native-cache adoption.
reviewed_controller_contract.shared_finance: Global atomic authority budget and physical-attempt limits cover all owners. Owner ceilings are not additive funds; pending/unknown liability or an overrun blocks new dispatch. Known completed receipt replay remains reusable.
